paragraphs: Friend, here is what I want you to carry out of this one. Hezekiah doesn't start by planning a parade or a program. He starts by opening and repairing the doors (2 Chronicles 29:3), then he tells the Levites to remove "every impurity" (2 Chronicles 29:5). Before anything new can be offered to the LORD, the house has to be made ready.

And look at how honest he is about it. He says plainly that their fathers were unfaithful and turned their backs on the LORD (2 Chronicles 29:6). Then he says, "Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel" (2 Chronicles 29:10). I spent years in the dark of a drawer, so I'll tell you this: facing the dark honestly is where the turning begins, and it starts in the heart.

Then the text shows what a ready house leads to. Atonement is made for all Israel (2 Chronicles 29:24), the singers sing, and the king and everyone with him bow down and worship (2 Chronicles 29:28-29). In the end "Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had prepared for the people" (2 Chronicles 29:36). So, baker, ask what in your own life needs its doors opened and its clutter carried out, because God has already prepared joy for the ones who turn back to Him.
